title: Dynamics of low energy wave packets in the one-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
authors: Mateusz Kwaśnicki, Marcin Napiórkowski, Sören Petrat, Michał Pietruszka
abstract: Spin wave theory plays a central role in the analysis of low-energy properties of the quantum ferromagnetic Heisenberg model. In this work, we present a first step towards a rigorous justification of this approximation in the context of quantum dynamics in one dimension. According to spin wave theory, the evolution of a spin wave state should be well approximated by its free evolution with the appropriate energy of free quasiparticles called magnons. Our main result establishes this idea rigorously for a class of spin wave packets. We focus on spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ systems, and consider wave packets composed of two magnons. We argue our result is optimal with respect to the timescales.
summary: This paper rigorously justifies the use of spin-wave theory for describing low-energy quantum dynamics in the 1D Heisenberg ferromagnet. By analyzing the difference between the exact and free time evolution for two-magnon wave packets, the authors establish a quantitative bound on the approximation error. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding magnetic excitations in quantum materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to provide a rigorous mathematical justification for using spin-wave theory to describe the low-energy quantum dynamics of the one-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet.
main_result: The authors establish a quantitative bound showing that the difference between the exact time evolution and the free evolution of two-magnon wave packets decays according to a specific functional form involving time and system size.
method: The analysis combines techniques from integrable systems, functional analysis, and harmonic analysis, focusing on bounding the norm difference between the exact and approximate time evolution operators.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on a 1D lattice. The dynamics are governed by the Hamiltonian $H_{\Lambda} = \sum_{\langle x,yangle \subset \Lambda} (S^2 - \mathbf{S}_x \cdot \mathbf{S}_y)$, and the focus is on low-energy excitations (magnons) in the two-magnon sector.
key_observables: The norm distance $\lVert \Psi_t^K - \Psi_{t, 	ext{free}}^K Vert^2_{\mathcal{H}_\Lambda}$ between the exact and free time evolutions.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the thermodynamic limit ($|\Lambda| 	o \infty$), for small momentum spread ($\epsilon$), and restricted to the two-magnon sector.
main_assumptions: The initial state must satisfy specific constraints related to the momentum spread $\epsilon$, and the result is restricted to the two-magnon subspace.
paper_structure: The paper develops the rigorous bound by analyzing the difference between the exact and free evolution, utilizing the integrable structure of the two-magnon sector and employing advanced mathematical tools like the Periodic Discrete Hilbert Transform.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for a standard approximation (spin-wave theory) used extensively in condensed matter physics to study magnetic excitations, which is crucial for understanding many-body dynamics.
